reference_documents.title: Standard Case Definitions for Priority Diseases in Kenya - IDSR
reference_documents.notes: Case definitions extracted and integrated into this JSON

_metadata.notes: Enhanced schema supports structured case definitions. Update and run: python manage.py seed_notifiable_diseases --update

diseases.name: Cholera
diseases.description: Acute diarrheal disease caused by Vibrio cholerae

case_definition.suspected: A patient aged 2 years or more with acute watery diarrhea with or without vomiting OR any patient with acute watery diarrhea dying within 2 hours of admission
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation of Vibrio cholerae O1 or O139
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IDSR Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Stool sample (rectal swab if stool not available)
laboratory_criteria.test: Culture for Vibrio cholerae O1 or O139

diseases.name: Yellow Fever
diseases.description: Viral hemorrhagic fever transmitted by mosquitoes

case_definition.suspected: Acute onset of fever followed by jaundice within 2 weeks of onset
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation (IgM antibodies, viral isolation, or PCR)
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IDSR Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.test: Yellow Fever IgM ELISA, PRNT, PCR, or viral isolation

diseases.name: Plague
diseases.description: Bacterial infection caused by Yersinia pestis

case_definition.suspected: Rapid onset of fever, chills, headache, severe malaise with painful lymphadenitis (bubonic) or pneumonia (pneumonic)
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation (isolation of Y. pestis or F1 antigen detection)
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IDSR Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Bubo aspirate, blood, sputum, or CSF
laboratory_criteria.test: Culture, F1 antigen detection, or PCR

diseases.name: Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers
diseases.description: Group of illnesses caused by several families of viruses (Ebola, Marburg, Lassa, etc.)

case_definition.suspected: Acute onset of fever and hemorrhagic manifestations (bleeding from gums, nose, injection sites, bloody stool/vomit) with no known predisposing host factors
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation (PCR, viral isolation, or specific IgM)
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IDSR Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Whole blood (EDTA), serum - handle with BSL-4 precautions
laboratory_criteria.test: RT-PCR, viral isolation, IgM ELISA

diseases.name: Measles
diseases.description: Highly contagious viral disease

case_definition.suspected: Any person with fever AND maculopapular (non-vesicular) rash AND cough, coryza (runny nose), or conjunctivitis (red eyes)
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with positive measles IgM OR epidemiological link to confirmed case

laboratory_criteria.test: Measles IgM ELISA, RT-PCR for viral RNA

diseases.name: Acute Flaccid Paralysis (Polio)
diseases.description: Any case of acute flaccid paralysis in a child under 15 years

case_definition.suspected: Any child under 15 years of age with sudden onset of flaccid paralysis in one or more limbs, OR any person of any age with paralytic illness if polio is suspected
case_definition.confirmed: AFP case with wild poliovirus or vaccine-derived poliovirus isolated from stool
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, WHO GPEI

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Two stool samples collected 24-48 hours apart within 14 days of paralysis onset
laboratory_criteria.test: Viral isolation and intratypic differentiation

diseases.name: Meningococcal Meningitis
diseases.description: Bacterial meningitis caused by Neisseria meningitidis

case_definition.suspected: Sudden onset of fever (>38.5C rectal or >38C axillary) AND one of: neck stiffness, altered consciousness, other meningeal sign, OR petechial/purpuric rash
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation (isolation, detection by PCR, or antigen detection)
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IDSR Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.test: Culture, Gram stain, latex agglutination, PCR

diseases.name: Rabies (Human)
diseases.description: Viral disease transmitted through bites from infected animals

case_definition.suspected: Acute encephalomyelitis (encephalitis) with history of animal bite or scratch, or exposure to saliva of suspected rabid animal
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation (direct fluorescent antibody test, PCR, or virus isolation)
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IDSR Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Saliva, CSF, skin biopsy (nuchal), brain tissue (post-mortem)
laboratory_criteria.test: Direct fluorescent antibody (DFA), RT-PCR, virus isolation

diseases.name: Diphtheria
diseases.description: Bacterial infection causing thick membrane in nose and throat

case_definition.suspected: Upper respiratory tract illness with grayish-white adherent membrane of pharynx, larynx, tonsils, or nose
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with isolation of toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae from clinical specimen
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IDSR Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Throat/nasopharyngeal swab (from beneath membrane if possible)
laboratory_criteria.test: Culture on Loeffler's medium, PCR for toxin gene

diseases.name: Neonatal Tetanus
diseases.description: Tetanus occurring in neonates

case_definition.suspected: Any neonate with normal ability to suck and cry during the first 2 days of life, AND between 3-28 days of age becomes unable to suck normally AND becomes stiff and/or has spasms
case_definition.confirmed: Clinical diagnosis (no laboratory confirmation required)

laboratory_criteria.test: No laboratory test required; diagnosis is clinical

diseases.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
diseases.description: Highly contagious respiratory disease caused by Bordetella pertussis

case_definition.suspected: A person with cough lasting 2+ weeks with at least one of: paroxysms (fits) of coughing, inspiratory whoop, post-tussive vomiting, without other apparent cause
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation (culture or PCR positive for B. pertussis)

laboratory_criteria.test: Culture, PCR

diseases.name: Anthrax
diseases.description: Bacterial disease caused by Bacillus anthracis

case_definition.suspected: Cutaneous: Skin lesion evolving from papule to vesicle to depressed black eschar, usually with edema. Inhalation: Acute onset, initial flu-like illness followed by severe respiratory distress. GI: Severe abdominal distress followed by fever and septicemia. All forms with history of exposure to infected animals or animal products.
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation (isolation of B. anthracis, or positive PCR, or positive serology)
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IDSR Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Vesicle fluid, eschar, blood, CSF, pleural fluid, stool, or sputum
laboratory_criteria.test: Culture, PCR, direct fluorescent antibody

diseases.name: SARS/Novel Coronavirus
diseases.description: Severe acute respiratory syndrome caused by novel coronaviruses

case_definition.suspected: A person with acute respiratory illness (fever and at least one sign/symptom of respiratory disease, e.g., cough, shortness of breath) AND with history of travel or residence in location reporting community transmission, OR close contact with confirmed case in the 14 days prior to symptom onset
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation by RT-PCR

laboratory_criteria.test: RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2

diseases.name: Influenza (Novel/Pandemic)
diseases.description: Novel or pandemic influenza strains

case_definition.suspected: Severe acute respiratory illness (SARI): Acute respiratory infection with fever 38C+, cough, onset within last 10 days, and requiring hospitalization
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation by RT-PCR or viral culture positive for novel influenza virus

laboratory_criteria.test: RT-PCR, viral culture

diseases.name: Smallpox
diseases.description: Eradicated disease - any suspected case requires immediate reporting

case_definition.suspected: Acute onset of fever >38.3C followed by a rash characterized by firm, deep-seated vesicles or pustules in the same stage of development, typically centrifugal distribution
case_definition.confirmed: PCR or electron microscopy confirmation of variola virus

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Vesicle fluid, scabs - handle with extreme caution
laboratory_criteria.test: PCR, electron microscopy - WHO reference lab only

diseases.name: Malaria
diseases.description: Parasitic disease transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes

case_definition.suspected: Any person with fever or history of fever within 48 hours (or presence of anemia in endemic areas)
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation (positive blood smear or RDT for Plasmodium species)

laboratory_criteria.test: Blood smear microscopy (thick and thin films), RDT

diseases.name: Typhoid Fever
diseases.description: Bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi

case_definition.suspected: Gradual onset of steadily increasing and then persistently high fever, chills, malaise, headache, sore throat, cough, and sometimes abdominal pain and constipation or diarrhea
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with isolation of Salmonella typhi from blood, stool, urine, or bone marrow
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IDSR Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Blood (first week), stool/urine (second week onwards), bone marrow
laboratory_criteria.test: Culture (gold standard), Widal test (supportive only)

diseases.name: Dysentery
diseases.description: Bloody diarrhea caused by Shigella or Entamoeba histolytica

case_definition.suspected: Acute diarrhea with visible blood in stool
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation (isolation of Shigella or identification of E. histolytica trophozoites)
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IDSR Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.test: Stool culture for Shigella, microscopy for E. histolytica

diseases.name: Tuberculosis
diseases.description: Bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis

case_definition.suspected: A person with cough for 2+ weeks with or without: weight loss, night sweats, fever, hemoptysis, chest pain, loss of appetite
case_definition.confirmed: Bacteriologically confirmed: positive sputum smear, culture, or GeneXpert MTB/RIF. Clinically diagnosed: diagnosed by clinician but not bacteriologically confirmed.

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Sputum (2 samples), gastric lavage, BAL, tissue
laboratory_criteria.test: Sputum smear microscopy (ZN/FM), GeneXpert MTB/RIF, culture

diseases.name: Acute Respiratory Infections (ARI)
diseases.description: Acute infections of the respiratory tract

case_definition.suspected: Sudden onset of fever with cough or sore throat or difficulty breathing
case_definition.confirmed: Clinical diagnosis; laboratory confirmation not routinely required
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IMCI Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.test: Clinical diagnosis primarily; viral panel if severe

diseases.name: Pneumonia
diseases.description: Lower respiratory tract infection

case_definition.suspected: Cough or difficulty breathing with fast breathing (age-specific cutoffs) with or without chest indrawing, fever, inability to drink
case_definition.confirmed: Clinical diagnosis with or without chest X-ray; culture if severe
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IMCI Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.test: Chest X-ray, sputum culture, blood culture

diseases.name: Diarrhea (Non-Bloody)
diseases.description: Acute diarrhea without blood

case_definition.suspected: Three or more loose or watery stools in a 24-hour period without visible blood
case_definition.confirmed: Clinical diagnosis; laboratory not routinely required
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IMCI Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.test: Stool culture, microscopy

diseases.name: Leprosy
diseases.description: Chronic bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium leprae

case_definition.suspected: Hypopigmented or reddish skin patch(es) with definite loss of sensation AND/OR peripheral nerve damage (thickening with loss of sensation and/or weakness)
case_definition.confirmed: Clinical diagnosis with positive skin smear (if available)

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Skin slit smear from earlobe, elbow, lesion
laboratory_criteria.test: Microscopy for acid-fast bacilli

diseases.name: Brucellosis
diseases.description: Bacterial zoonotic disease

case_definition.suspected: Acute or insidious onset of intermittent or remittent fever, night sweats, fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, headache, arthralgia, with history of contact with infected animals or consumption of unpasteurized dairy products
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with isolation of Brucella species OR positive serology (SAT 1:160+ OR 4-fold rise in titer)
case_definition.source: MOH Standard Case Definitions, IDSR Guidelines

laboratory_criteria.test: Blood culture, SAT (Standard Agglutination Test), ELISA

diseases.name: Tetanus (Non-Neonatal)
diseases.description: Bacterial disease causing muscle stiffness and spasms

case_definition.suspected: Acute onset of hypertonia and/or painful muscular contractions (usually of muscles of jaw and neck) and generalized muscle spasms without other apparent medical cause
case_definition.confirmed: Clinical diagnosis (no laboratory confirmation required)

laboratory_criteria.test: No laboratory test required; diagnosis is clinical. May test wound for C. tetani

diseases.name: Hepatitis (Viral)
diseases.description: Inflammation of the liver caused by hepatitis viruses

case_definition.suspected: Acute illness with discrete onset of symptoms AND jaundice OR elevated serum aminotransferase levels >2.5x upper limit of normal
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with positive serological markers (HAV IgM, HBsAg, HCV Ab, HEV IgM)

laboratory_criteria.test: HAV IgM, HBsAg, Anti-HBc IgM, HCV Ab, HEV IgM, LFTs

diseases.name: Chikungunya
diseases.description: Viral disease transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes

case_definition.suspected: Acute onset of fever >38.5C AND severe arthralgia/arthritis not explained by other medical conditions, in a resident or visitor to endemic areas
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with positive PCR, virus isolation, or IgM seroconversion/4-fold rise in IgG

laboratory_criteria.test: RT-PCR (acute), IgM ELISA (after day 5), PRNT

diseases.name: Dengue Fever
diseases.description: Viral disease transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes

case_definition.suspected: Acute febrile illness with two or more of: headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, arthralgia, rash, hemorrhagic manifestations, leukopenia
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with laboratory confirmation (NS1, PCR, IgM seroconversion, or virus isolation)

laboratory_criteria.test: NS1 antigen, RT-PCR, IgM/IgG ELISA, virus isolation

diseases.name: Rift Valley Fever
diseases.description: Viral zoonotic disease affecting humans and livestock

case_definition.suspected: Acute onset of fever with hemorrhagic manifestations, jaundice, or encephalitis AND history of contact with sick/dead animals or residence in area with animal disease outbreak
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with positive PCR, virus isolation, or seroconversion (4-fold IgG rise or IgM positive)

laboratory_criteria.test: RT-PCR, IgM ELISA, virus isolation

diseases.name: Trypanosomiasis (Sleeping Sickness)
diseases.description: Parasitic disease caused by Trypanosoma species

case_definition.suspected: Person with intermittent fever in endemic area AND one or more of: chancre at bite site, lymphadenopathy (especially posterior cervical), headache, sleep disturbance, behavioral changes
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with identification of trypanosomes in blood, lymph node aspirate, or CSF

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Blood (thick smear), lymph node aspirate, CSF (for staging)
laboratory_criteria.test: CATT (Card Agglutination Test), wet mount microscopy, CSF examination

diseases.name: Leishmaniasis (Kala-azar)
diseases.description: Parasitic disease transmitted by sandflies

case_definition.suspected: Person from endemic area with prolonged fever (>2 weeks), weight loss, hepatomegaly and/or splenomegaly, and pancytopenia
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with demonstration of parasites in tissue (spleen, bone marrow, lymph node) OR positive serology (rK39) with compatible clinical picture

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Splenic aspirate, bone marrow aspirate, lymph node aspirate
laboratory_criteria.test: rK39 RDT, direct microscopy (Giemsa stain), PCR

diseases.name: Schistosomiasis (Bilharzia)
diseases.description: Parasitic disease caused by blood flukes

case_definition.suspected: Person with history of freshwater contact in endemic area with hematuria (urinary) OR bloody diarrhea/abdominal pain (intestinal)
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with detection of Schistosoma eggs in urine or stool

laboratory_criteria.test: Urine filtration/microscopy, Kato-Katz thick smear

diseases.name: Trachoma
diseases.description: Bacterial eye infection caused by Chlamydia trachomatis

case_definition.suspected: Active trachoma (TF/TI): Presence of 5+ follicles (0.5mm+) in upper tarsal conjunctiva OR trachomatous inflammation-intense with thickening obscuring >50% tarsal vessels
case_definition.confirmed: Clinical diagnosis using WHO simplified grading system; no routine laboratory confirmation

laboratory_criteria.test: PCR for C. trachomatis (not routine)

diseases.name: Onchocerciasis (River Blindness)
diseases.description: Parasitic disease transmitted by blackflies

case_definition.suspected: Person in endemic area with chronic itching/dermatitis, subcutaneous nodules (onchocercomata), AND/OR visual impairment not explained by other causes
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with identification of microfilariae in skin snips OR adult worms in nodule

laboratory_criteria.specimen: Skin snip from iliac crest or scapula
laboratory_criteria.test: Microscopy for microfilariae

diseases.name: Lymphatic Filariasis
diseases.description: Parasitic disease transmitted by mosquitoes causing elephantiasis

case_definition.suspected: Person in endemic area with lymphedema/elephantiasis of limbs, hydrocele (scrotal swelling), acute dermatolymphangioadenitis (ADLA), or chyluria
case_definition.confirmed: A suspected case with detection of microfilariae in night blood OR positive antigen test (ICT card)

laboratory_criteria.test: Thick blood smear microscopy, ICT antigen card test

diseases.name: Maternal Deaths
diseases.description: Death of a woman during pregnancy or within 42 days of termination

case_definition.suspected: Death of a woman while pregnant or within 42 days of termination of pregnancy, irrespective of the duration and site of the pregnancy, from any cause related to or aggravated by the pregnancy or its management
case_definition.confirmed: Maternal death confirmed through Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response (MPDSR)

laboratory_criteria.test: N/A - verbal autopsy and clinical review

diseases.name: Perinatal Deaths
diseases.description: Death from 22 weeks gestation to 7 days after birth

case_definition.suspected: Stillbirth: Death of fetus from 22 completed weeks of gestation (or birth weight 500g+) before birth. Early neonatal death: Death of live-born infant within first 7 days of life.
case_definition.confirmed: Perinatal death confirmed through MPDSR review

laboratory_criteria.test: N/A - verbal autopsy and clinical review

diseases.name: Severe Acute Malnutrition
diseases.description: Severe wasting or nutritional edema in children

case_definition.suspected: Child 6-59 months with: MUAC <11.5cm, OR weight-for-height/length <-3 Z-scores, OR bilateral pitting edema
case_definition.confirmed: Anthropometric confirmation using WHO growth standards

laboratory_criteria.test: MUAC tape, length/height board, weighing scale

diseases.name: Animal Bites
diseases.description: Bites from dogs, cats, monkeys, or other animals (potential rabies exposure)

case_definition.suspected: Person bitten or scratched by any animal (domestic or wild) that breaks the skin or mucosa
case_definition.confirmed: Clinical assessment of bite wound with PEP assessment

laboratory_criteria.specimen: N/A for patient (animal brain if available)
laboratory_criteria.test: DFA on animal brain tissue (post-mortem)

diseases.name: Snake Bites
diseases.description: Venomous or non-venomous snake bites

case_definition.suspected: History of snake bite with or without: fang marks, local pain/swelling, bleeding, neurological symptoms, or systemic symptoms
case_definition.confirmed: Clinical diagnosis; snake identification if possible

laboratory_criteria.test: 20-minute whole blood clotting test (20WBCT), PT/INR, FBC
